map: Theorem 3.1 printed argument: for lambda_n→bar_lambda, boundedness of w_{lambda_n} supplies convergent subsequences. Passing the inequalities L_{lambda_n}(w_{lambda_n})≤L_{lambda_n}(w) to the limit for each fixed w shows every cluster point minimizes L_{bar_lambda}. Uniqueness identifies it with w_{bar_lambda}. Boundedness and the unique cluster point yield convergence of the sequence. Joint continuity of E gives continuity of f, and compactness gives existence.

Theorem 3.2 printed argument: a common nu gives |f_T(lambda)-f(lambda)|≤nu||w_{T,lambda}-w_lambda|| for all T,lambda. Assumption (vi) gives uniform convergence of f_T to f. The paper then invokes Theorem A.1 for minima and minimizer cluster points.

Theorem A.1 printed Proof in the continuous-limit setting: compactness supplies a convergent subsequence of minimizers. Uniform convergence bounds |phi_{K_T}(lambda_{K_T})-phi(lambda_{K_T})| by the uniform error. Continuity of phi and minimizing inequalities against each fixed lambda identify the limit as a minimizer and yield convergence of the corresponding minimum values. A further-subsequence contradiction using Eq.(11) establishes convergence of the full minimum-value sequence.

assumptions: Theorem 3.1 (i): Lambda is compact. Nonemptiness is the implicit feasibility convention needed for existence; it is explicitly disclosed here rather than attributed to the printed wording of (i).
Theorem 3.1 (iii): (w,lambda)↦L_lambda(w) is jointly continuous, and argmin_{u in R^d} L_lambda(u) is a singleton for every lambda in Lambda.

Theorem 3.2 additionally (v): there exists finite nu>0 independent of lambda such that |E(w,lambda)-E(v,lambda)|≤nu||w-v|| for all w,v in R^d and lambda in Lambda. This uniform-in-lambda interpretation is explicit in its Appendix A Proof.
Theorem 3.2 additionally (vi): sup_{lambda in Lambda}||w_{T,lambda}-w_lambda||→0 as T→infinity. The approximants are those of the continuous finite dynamics in Eqs.(5),(6).
statement.conclusion: Theorem 3.1: under (i)–(iv), f attains a global minimum on Lambda. Theorem 3.2: with the additional conditions, inf_Lambda f_T→inf_Lambda f. For every selection lambda_T in argmin_Lambda f_T, the sequence admits a convergent subsequence; every convergent subsequence lambda_{K_T}→bar_lambda satisfies bar_lambda in argmin_Lambda f. The notation argmin f_T→argmin f has precisely this sequential meaning. It does not assert Hausdorff convergence, approximation of every minimizer of f, uniqueness, or convergence of an arbitrary entire minimizer sequence.
statement.objects_and_definitions: Finite-dimensional Euclidean spaces R^m and R^d, with norm ||.||. For a nonempty set Lambda⊂R^m, let w_lambda be the unique global minimizer of L_lambda:R^d→R. Define f(lambda)=E(w_lambda,lambda), Eq.(7), and f_T(lambda)=E(w_{T,lambda},lambda), Eq.(5). The finite approximants follow Eq.(6): w_{0,lambda}=Phi_0(lambda), w_{t,lambda}=Phi_t(w_{t-1,lambda},lambda), with smooth Phi_0:R^m→R^d and Phi_t:R^d×R^m→R^d. In particular each finite approximant is continuous in lambda. Every outer infimum and argmin below is over the same Lambda.
statement.parameter_domains: d,m are finite positive integers; T ranges through positive integers and tends to infinity. Lambda is fixed, nonempty and compact. nu is finite and independent of T and lambda. No accuracy-dependent iteration budget or convergence rate is asserted.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every family satisfying (i)–(iv), Theorem 3.1 applies. For every sequence of approximants in the Eq.(6) setting satisfying additional (v),(vi), Theorem 3.2 applies. Its minimizer conclusion holds for every choice lambda_T in argmin_Lambda f_T and every convergent subsequence thereof. These are deterministic statements; no stochastic convergence or sampling probability is asserted.
